briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The past 24 hours saw a notable cessation of overt US military strikes against Iran, ending a nearly two-week daily engagement, coinciding with Omani-mediated talks in Tehran concerning the Strait of Hormuz. Despite this diplomatic opening, President Trump maintains the option for "full-scale war" if demands are not met, while Iran continues to issue stern warnings against US allies and demonstrates sustained retaliatory capabilities.

IRAN
Military operations in and against Iran:
The US paused its daily strikes against Iran for the first time in 13 nights on Friday, July 24, with President Trump citing a desire to allow for diplomacy and an assessment that the current level of strikes had reached its effectiveness limit. Iran's official media reported explosions near Bandar Abbas, though a senior US official denied any American attack in that area. Ukraine, via President Zelensky, claimed its forces attacked an Iranian-linked commercial vessel in the Caspian Sea on Saturday morning, July 25, alleging it was transporting military cargo to Russia. Iran confirmed this attack resulted in an explosion, killing one sailor and injuring another, condemning it as an "act of aggression" that could "aggravate and expand the war" and summoning Ukraine's Chargé d'Affaires. The IRGC spokesman, Sardar Mohhebi, claimed Iranian forces destroyed 11 US fighter jets/helicopters on the ground and 17 US spy/strike drones over 15 days (July 17-31), asserting US casualty figures were "an absolute lie" with over 200 alleged US deaths. Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, declared that strikes against US targets will continue until the "enemy’s total surrender" to "avenge the massacre of children in Minab and Lamerd." Iran also reported that damage to tunnels, bridges, and roads from bombing attacks had been repaired and reopened in less than 12 hours. Reports indicate residents in the port city of Jask are patrolling with weapons, anticipating US forces. The US military disabled two commercial ships, M/T Lavine (Mozambique flag) in the Gulf of Oman on July 24 and M/T Charminar (Comoros flag) in the Arabian Sea on July 25, for repeatedly attempting to violate the maritime blockade on Iran. Reports suggest Iran is increasingly using Khaibarshakan ballistic missiles with evolving tactics, with some penetrating US defenses.

Internal political situation:
Nournews, close to Iran's Supreme National Security Council, reported that a meeting targeted by US/Israel on March 9, which killed senior officials, was a subcommittee meeting of the Defense Council focused on "managing" popular protests.

Economic impact:
Iran faces a fuel crisis, with the National Oil Products Company urging public transport use due to shortages, and long queues for diesel in Tehran. Government spokesman Fatemeh Mohajerani stated changes in gasoline prices or quotas are "certain" to manage consumption. The Shahid Rajaee port, a key trade hub, is reportedly struggling with severely reduced container traffic.

Leadership decisions:
Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that the presence of US bases in the region is a source of insecurity and indicated Iran is open to dialogue if the US understands Iran's power. He also acknowledged Oman's role as a neutral mediator for talks on the Strait of Hormuz.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations:
Israel was on high alert, preparing for a potentially powerful US attack on Iran on Friday night/Saturday morning (July 24/25), even considering joining attacks if Tehran retaliated against Israel. An Israeli official admitted uncertainty regarding President Trump's precise plans. The US continues aerial transfers of planes and ammunition to Israel despite the pause in strikes on Iran.

Casualties:
An Israeli man, 25, was injured in the head by a stone during a violent confrontation near Susya in the southern West Bank, requiring hospitalization in moderate condition.

Home front air defense:
A drone fell near the home of National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir in Hebron; the circumstances are under investigation, but no injuries to the minister or his family were reported.

Political decisions:
Defense Minister Israel Katz met with administrative detainee Yinon Dardik, who is on a hunger strike and accused of abusing Palestinians. Katz offered house arrest as an alternative, which Dardik declined. The Central Command commander banned Palestinian laborers from entering all Israeli settlements due to escalating tensions in the West Bank. The Israeli cabinet held a five-hour emergency discussion on Friday night due to fears of a broad American attack on Iran. Opposition leader Yair Golan, in his campaign launch speech, criticized Netanyahu and Defense Minister Katz for turning Judea and Samaria into a "powder keg," calling for an end to "Jewish terror," dismantling Ben-Gvir's armed militias, and removing illegal outposts. Golan also outlined a platform to revoke judicial overhaul laws, establish an inquiry commission, and bar indicted individuals from government.

Civilian impact:
The US Embassy in Israel issued an emergency warning for US citizens to prepare for a sudden escalation. ITA Airways and Austrian Airlines have cancelled flights to Israel until at least Tuesday due to security concerns. Protests against the government and judicial reform took place at dozens of locations in northern Israel. Demonstrators gathered outside PM Netanyahu's "seventh secret residence" in Jerusalem, blaming him for the October 7 events. WhatsApp blocking for many Israelis prompted the Israeli Internet Association to contact Meta.

Strategic objectives:
Israeli officials assess that Trump's pause in strikes offers Iran only a temporary reprieve, believing a permanent agreement meeting US demands is highly unlikely.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Ground operations:
IDF troops are deployed in the Gaza Strip. The IDF conducted counter-terrorism operations in the West Bank, arresting over 70 wanted individuals and interrogating hundreds.

Casualties:
In central Gaza on Monday, July 20, the IDF killed Muhannad Asaad Mahmoud Abu Ghazal, a Hamas Nukhba Force commander involved in the October 7 Kissufim raid. In northern Gaza on Tuesday, July 21, the IDF killed Raed Hani Mohammed, a Hamas aerial surveillance operative, and Nabhan Mohammed Nabhan al-Amsi, chief of intelligence in Hamas's Gaza City Brigade, targeting them for advancing terror plots. Gaza sources reported the killing of Brigadier General Abdel-Nasser Al-Maqadma, the police chief in northern Gaza, in an airstrike in Sheikh Radwan, along with at least four others. The Gaza Health Ministry claimed 6 Palestinians were killed and 37 injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza over the past 48 hours.

Humanitarian situation:
No specific details on the humanitarian situation were provided beyond casualty figures.

Ceasefire or negotiation status:
No direct information on a specific ceasefire or negotiation status for Gaza/West Bank was available.

Settler activity:
A violent confrontation occurred near the Susya settlement in the southern West Bank, involving stone-throwing between Israeli civilians and Palestinians. A Palestinian snatched a weapon from an Israeli civilian (an off-duty soldier), fired it in the air, and fled. An Israeli man, 25, was injured in the head by a stone. The weapon was recovered, and the perpetrator was later arrested by Border Police. The commander of the Central Command banned Palestinian laborers from entering all Israeli settlements due to escalating tensions. The Arab Parliament and UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese condemned the surge in Israeli settler violence in the occupied West Bank, demanding accountability.

LEBANON
Hezbollah operations:
A Hezbollah official stated that if Israel launches a "direct attack on Iran," Hezbollah will "enter the battle fully."

Israeli strikes:
Israeli forces reportedly burned and demolished homes in southern Lebanon while carrying out military aggression across the border region. Israeli forces' artillery shelled the southern Lebanese town of Markaba and the Ali al-Taher heights. Lebanese media clarified that reports of rocket launches from southern Lebanon were false, indicating that smoke and phosphorus bombs were observed near Kfartibnit.

UNIFIL incidents:
No incidents involving UNIFIL were reported.

Displacement:
No displacement figures were reported.

Cross-border exchanges:
Initial reports of gunfire from southern Lebanon towards Israeli areas were later clarified as non-rocket related.

GULF STATES
Military posture:
Yemen's Houthis claimed two "qualitative military operations" targeting sensitive Saudi Aramco facilities in Jizan and Yanbu provinces with dozens of ballistic missiles and drones. This was in retaliation for Saudi airstrikes on Hudaydah city and Kamaran Island in Yemen. The Saudi Press Agency confirmed that the Saudi-owned tanker NCC Masa sustained minor hull damage in a Red Sea attack on Friday, but continued its journey safely. The Yemeni armed forces spokesperson stated that the maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia remains in place, vowing "escalation for escalation" and to expand operations if the Saudi siege continues. Houthis accused the Saudi government of refusing demands to lift the blockade on Yemen. Satellite imagery reportedly captured the aftermath of Iranian retaliatory strikes targeting Amazon servers and a data center in western Bahrain. Kuwait's ambassador to Washington denied a Wall Street Journal report claiming Kuwait participated in military operations against Iran, labeling the claim as "baseless" and asserting that Kuwait does not permit the use of its territory, airspace, or waters for offensive operations against neighbors.

Diplomacy:
An Omani delegation arrived in Tehran on Friday for talks on a new arrangement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, with reports suggesting progress and a potential agreement by the end of the weekend. Qatar's Ministry of Transport announced that maritime traffic will fully resume on July 26. Saudi Foreign Minister held a phone call with his Pakistani counterpart to discuss efforts to de-escalate regional tensions and secure waterways. IRGC Quds Force Commander Brigadier General Esmaeil Qaani urged the Saudi government to learn from America's "unwise and costly behavior" and end the 11-year blockade on Yemen. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman, Ismail Baghaei, stressed that the Yemen crisis has no military solution, advocating for dialogue and a full implementation of the agreed roadmap.

Economic impact:
Ship insurers have restricted war coverage for Saudi-linked vessels in the Red Sea following Yemeni attacks, increasing risks to Saudi oil exports. The UAE's Habshan-Fujairah pipeline is highlighted as a strategic asset, allowing the country to navigate the Hormuz crisis more effectively than neighbors.

Strait of Hormuz implications:
The potential Omani-Iranian agreement focuses on reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Speaker of the National Security Commission, Ghashghavi, stressed that the Strait of Hormuz will never return to its pre-war conditions and will only reopen with Iran's armed forces' permission.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Militia activity:
In Iraq, security forces were deployed to Sadr City in Baghdad, known as a launching point for missiles and drones, to confront pro-Iranian militias. Initial reports indicated armed clashes between Hashed al-Shaabi and the Iraqi Army over attempts by the army to seize drones from Hashed al-Shaabi bases, followed by reports of the Iraqi Army mobilizing columns towards Hashed al-Shaabi headquarters. The Iraqi Resistance (Saraya Awliya al-Dam) denied involvement in recent attacks on Erbil and Kuwait.

Airstrikes:
An unidentified drone was shot down by air defense near the US Consulate in Erbil, northern Iraq. Satellite imagery reportedly captured the direct impact point of Iranian retaliatory strikes on what appeared to be fuel bladders at the Muwaffaq Al-Salti US Air Base in Jordan.

Spillover effects:
A massive explosion and large fire were reported at the Jambur oil field in Kirkuk province, northern Iraq, with initial reports linking it to an Emirati company. Flights by A Jet and Royal Jordanian Airlines from Erbil International Airport were canceled. The US Embassy in Erbil issued a severe security warning due to recent Iranian strikes. Dozens of US military transport aircraft are frequently landing and taking off from Erbil International Airport.

Diplomatic developments:
Syrian President Ahmed al-Shara met with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres. The Iraqi Cabinet approved public holidays for Monday and Tuesday, August 3-4, 2026, to commemorate Arba'een.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **US Halts Strikes on Iran:** For the first time in 13 consecutive nights, the US military did not conduct new strikes in Iran on Friday, July 24, as ordered by President Trump to allow for diplomatic efforts.
2.  **Hormuz Diplomacy:** An Omani delegation arrived in Tehran on Friday, July 24, for talks on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, with regional sources indicating potential agreement by the end of the weekend.
3.  **Trump's "Full-Scale War" Threat:** President Trump stated he is "absolutely" considering resuming full-scale war against Iran "if we don't get 100% of what we want," despite the diplomatic pause.
4.  **Ukraine Attacks Iranian-Linked Ships in Caspian:** Ukrainian President Zelensky claimed Ukrainian forces attacked Iranian-linked commercial vessels in the Caspian Sea on Saturday morning, July 25, alleging they transported military cargo to Russia. Iran confirmed one sailor was killed and another injured.
5.  **Hamas Commanders Eliminated:** The IDF announced the elimination of Muhannad Asaad Mahmoud Abu Ghazal, a Hamas Nukhba commander involved in the October 7 Kissufim raid, in central Gaza (Monday, July 20), along with two other Hamas intelligence and surveillance operatives in northern Gaza (Tuesday, July 21). Separately, Gaza sources reported the killing of Brigadier General Abdel-Nasser Al-Maqadma, the police chief in northern Gaza, in an airstrike in Sheikh Radwan.
6.  **West Bank Confrontation & Weapon Snatching:** A violent confrontation occurred near Susya in the southern West Bank, where a Palestinian snatched an off-duty Israeli soldier's weapon, fired it in the air, and fled. An Israeli man, 25, was injured by a stone. Border Police later arrested the suspect.
7.  **Houthi Attacks on Saudi Aramco:** Yemeni Houthis launched dozens of ballistic missiles and drones at sensitive Saudi Aramco facilities in Jizan and Yanbu provinces in Saudi Arabia, in retaliation for Saudi airstrikes on Hudaydah and Kamaran Island in Yemen.
8.  **IRGC Threats to US Allies:** The IRGC spokesman, Sardar Mohhebi, warned that any country supporting the US in the conflict, including the UK and Gulf states, would become a "legitimate target" for Iran.
9.  **Jambur Oil Field Explosion:** A massive explosion and large fire were reported at the Jambur oil field in Kirkuk province, northern Iraq, with initial reports linking it to an Emirati company.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks: Despite the temporary halt in US strikes, the risk of a regional escalation remains extremely high. President Trump's explicit threat of "full-scale war" if diplomatic demands are not fully met, coupled with Iran's firm stance on defending its interests and continuing "retaliatory strikes" until "total surrender," indicates a fragile diplomatic window. The IRGC's direct threats against the UK and Gulf states supporting the US further broaden the potential conflict zone. Ukraine's attack on Iranian-linked vessels in the Caspian Sea, condemned by Iran as an "act of aggression," adds another dimension of potential retaliation.
Active flashpoints: The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical flashpoint, with ongoing US maritime blockade enforcement (disabling two ships) and Omani-mediated talks for its reopening. Iran asserts it will only open with its permission. The Red Sea/Bab al-Mandab continues to see Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities and Saudi-linked tankers, maintaining high naval and economic risk. The West Bank faces persistent internal instability, as demonstrated by violent confrontations and a weapon snatching incident in Susya. Iraq is a volatile environment, with explosions at the Jambur oil field, reports of US military buildup in Erbil, and clashes between Iraqi security forces and pro-Iranian militias in Baghdad.
Military posture changes: US military assets in the region remain on high alert, with aircraft in combat-ready positions and increased tanker deployment. US continues to transfer military equipment to Israel. Iran claims to have rapidly repaired damaged infrastructure and boasts significant destruction of US air assets, while deploying advanced missile tactics. Saudi Arabia is conducting airstrikes in Yemen, and its Aramco facilities remain targets. Kuwait denies involvement in offensive operations, attempting to de-escalate.
Red lines: Iran's alleged attacks on US assets and its explicit threat of targeting any state aiding the US (including UK and Gulf states) indicate clear red lines regarding perceived support for US military actions. Trump's condition of "100% of what we want" for avoiding full-scale war, and the ongoing enforcement of the maritime blockade, represent US red lines.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
US posture: President Trump ordered a temporary pause in strikes on Iran, signaling a willingness for diplomacy but maintaining readiness for a "full-scale war" if demands are not met. He stated Iran is becoming "more serious" in talks. US Central Command confirmed continued enforcement of the maritime blockade, disabling two ships. US military continues to transfer military equipment to Israel.
Gulf states: Oman is actively mediating talks in Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Qatar announced a full resumption of maritime traffic from July 26. Kuwait's ambassador to Washington denied any participation in military operations against Iran. Saudi Arabia continues airstrikes in Yemen but is also engaged in diplomatic discussions with Pakistan. The UAE's Fujairah pipeline is highlighted as a strategic asset.
EU members: EU Foreign Policy Chief Kaja Kallas spoke with Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi. ITA Airways and Austrian Airlines cancelled flights to Israel. Belgium arrested a Canadian citizen of Chinese origin, an intern at NATO HQ, on espionage charges. France's embassy in Tehran strongly denied claims of secret meetings to pressure Iran.
Russia: President Zelensky claimed Russian satellites are assisting Tehran in Middle East attacks. Russia is reportedly preparing to bring 30,000 North Korean soldiers to Ukraine and extended its gasoline export ban until year-end.
China: China's crude imports plummeted due to the Hormuz crisis, but the country reportedly avoided an energy crisis due to strategic buffers.
Other: UN Secretary-General Guterres met Syrian President al-Shara. UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese condemned Israeli settler violence in the West Bank. The Arab Parliament also condemned the surge in settler violence. ICC Prosecutor Karim Khan was suspended amid sexual misconduct allegations. Brazil rejected visas for two US State Department officials who sought to influence the upcoming presidential elections.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Contradictory claims: Official Iranian media reported explosions near Bandar Abbas, but a senior US official denied any US attack. The Wall Street Journal reported Kuwaiti and Bahraini involvement in strikes against Iran, which was directly contradicted by Kuwait's ambassador. An IRGC spokesman's claim of "almost all US infrastructure in Erbil has been destroyed" contradicts other reports of active US military flights at Erbil airport. Conflicting reports exist on whether US preparedness for strikes on Iran was for a "wide-ranging attack" or attacks of the "same scope as every night in the last two weeks."
Unverified claims: The IRGC spokesman's claim of "over 200" US casualties is highly unlikely to be verifiable and is likely inflated for propaganda purposes. A claim that maritime shipping between China and Saudi Arabia has halted due to Houthi attacks lacks broader corroboration. The initial report linking the Jambur oil field explosion to an Emirati company needs further confirmation.
Propaganda indicators: IRGC claims of destroying numerous US air assets and inflicting high casualties are likely exaggerated. IRGC threats against the UK and Gulf states are intended to deter support for the US. The Gaza Health Ministry's reported death toll of 73,317 for the past 48 hours is a cumulative figure for the entire conflict, used for maximum emotional impact. Reports of residents in Jask patrolling with weapons for US forces serve as a message of defiance. President Trump's reported comment at the White House Correspondents' Dinner, referring to the current Iranian leadership as a "gay dictator" is inflammatory and designed to be provocative, regardless of its accuracy.
Reporting gaps: No independent verification of Ukrainian claims regarding attacks on Iranian-linked ships in the Caspian Sea or Russian satellite assistance to Iran. Specific details on the "demands" President Trump is making of Iran remain unclear. Limited independent verification of the scale of damage to US bases from alleged Iranian strikes. The precise nature and origin of the explosion at the Jambur oil field are not fully clear. No updates on internal dissent or anti-regime protests in Iran were provided.
